candidates.rule: Do not change the unique_id format of entities that already shipped; leave existing suffixes untouched and only apply a new scheme to newly added entities.
candidates.trigger: A diff edits the f-string that builds `_attr_unique_id` for an entity class that already exists in a released integration.

candidates.rule: Polling and update-interval constants must match the cadence stated in the integration's README, inline comments and the PR description; change the constant or the documentation so they agree.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds or changes a `*_UPDATE_DELAY` / `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES` / `SCAN_INTERVAL` constant to a value different from the interval documented for that integration.

candidates.rule: Device- or feature-specific trigger logic added to a shared entity class must be gated on the entity description key / event type it belongs to, not applied to every instance of the class.
candidates.trigger: A shared entity's _async_update_attrs stops consulting `self._event` (or the description key) and keys off a device-specific field such as `doorbell_seq` for all instances.

candidates.rule: A configuration entity whose value can be changed outside Home Assistant and receives no push updates must be disabled by default and set _attr_should_poll with a long SCAN_INTERVAL, mirroring the existing pattern in the integration.
candidates.trigger: A new EntityCategory.CONFIG number/select entity is added with neither _attr_should_poll/SCAN_INTERVAL nor entity_registry_enabled_default=False, while sibling config entities in the same integration set both.

candidates.rule: Entity names in strings.json must use sentence case, matching the surrounding entries.
candidates.trigger: A strings.json diff adds an entity `name` with title-cased words (e.g. "Sync Date and Time") while neighbouring names are sentence case.

candidates.rule: Changing which device types map to which entity descriptions requires tests that assert the exact entities created for each affected device type, not just that setup does not crash.
candidates.trigger: A diff edits a SENSOR_DESCRIPTIONS_BY_DEVICE_TYPES-style mapping (adding or removing a device type) with only a smoke/regression test that setup succeeds.

candidates.rule: Constants shared by more than one module of an integration belong in that integration's const.py and must not be duplicated across __init__.py and services.py.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a service constant or command map to __init__.py that already exists in services.py (or vice versa).

candidates.rule: Entity-registry migrations that match legacy unique_ids must derive the legacy prefix from the exact value that originally built those ids, and the tests must cover the case where that value differs from the config entry host.
candidates.trigger: A migration filters entity registry entries with `entity_entry.unique_id.startswith(config_entry.data[CONF_HOST])` when the old unique_id was built from a different source (API hostname, serial, etc.).

candidates.rule: value_fn lambdas in entity descriptions must match the signature of the helper they call; do not rely on the platform's TypeError handling in native_value to absorb a mismatch.
candidates.trigger: An entity description passes `value=lambda data, k=...: helper(data, k)` while the helper is declared to take a different argument (e.g. a single typed object).

candidates.rule: Do not override async_toggle on light entities; rely on the default ToggleEntity implementation that calls async_turn_on/async_turn_off.
candidates.trigger: A light platform defines `async def async_toggle` that forwards to a device/library toggle call.

candidates.rule: Code that reads coordinator data must match the payload shape actually stored in coordinator.data (as shown by the diagnostics snapshots); convert payloads into typed objects consistently before storing them rather than assuming attributes on raw dicts.
candidates.trigger: A helper iterates `self.data["..."].values()` and accesses attributes (`zone_data.ac_power`) on entries the coordinator stores as raw API dicts.

candidates.rule: Never call a synchronous vendor-library method directly from async code; wrap it in hass.async_add_executor_job (or expose it as a non-async accessor), especially when the same call is already treated as blocking elsewhere in the integration.
candidates.trigger: An `async def` method returns or awaits the result of a sync library call such as `self._tado.rate_limit_info()` with no executor job.

candidates.rule: An entity factory must not return None for arbitrary unknown description keys; restrict the skip to the intended conditional entities and log or raise for keys that are missing from the mapping.
candidates.trigger: A create_sensor/create_entity helper gains a broad `if key not in self.services: return None` guard in front of the mapping lookup.

candidates.rule: When a device response is missing the key backing an entity state, report unknown (return None) rather than defaulting to the off/false state.
candidates.trigger: A state property does `return result.get("SomeKey") == "0"` or `bool(data.get(key, False))` so an absent key becomes a definite OFF.

candidates.rule: Sanitize any user-provided value used as a statistic_id prefix (slugify or replace separators such as '-'), do not merely lowercase it, before calling async_add_external_statistics.
candidates.trigger: A coordinator builds a statistic_id from config entry data with `.lower()` or direct interpolation and passes it to async_add_external_statistics / async_import_statistics.

candidates.rule: Integration service handlers must raise ServiceValidationError when the config entry they need is missing or not loaded, instead of failing with a generic or unhandled error.
candidates.trigger: A service handler resolves a config entry (or requires a loaded entry) and raises HomeAssistantError, asserts, or proceeds without a ServiceValidationError path.

candidates.rule: Every reason passed to async_abort in a config flow or subentry flow must have a key in that flow's `abort` block in strings.json; keys defined only under `error` are not used for aborts.
candidates.trigger: A flow calls `self.async_abort(reason="cannot_connect")` (or similar) while strings.json defines that key only under `config_subentries.<type>.error` / `config.error`.

candidates.rule: Register the teardown of any connection or resource opened in async_setup_entry with entry.async_on_unload (or close it in the failure path) before calling async_config_entry_first_refresh.
candidates.trigger: async_setup_entry opens a client/connection, then calls async_config_entry_first_refresh, with the close registered only in async_unload_entry.

candidates.rule: Test fixtures must mock the real shape of the vendor library's objects (typed objects, not dict stand-ins), so attribute-versus-item access mismatches fail in tests.
candidates.trigger: Integration code accesses a library value one way (e.g. `d["unique_id"]`) while tests/components/<domain>/ supply a plain dict/MagicMock that tolerates both shapes.

candidates.rule: Diagnostics code must use Home Assistant's shared redaction helpers and REDACTED constant rather than hard-coding a redaction marker string.
candidates.trigger: A diagnostics.py module writes a literal like `"**REDACTED**"` in a custom scrubbing function instead of importing the constant used by async_redact_data.

candidates.rule: Pass only raw identifiers (entity_id, chat_id) in translation_placeholders and keep the explanatory wording inside the translation string itself.
candidates.trigger: A ServiceValidationError/HomeAssistantError raised with translation_placeholders whose value is an f-string containing English prose such as f"Notify entity not found: {entity_id}".

candidates.rule: When a shared config-flow helper such as validate_input gains a new branch, add test coverage for every flow that calls it, including reauth.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds a fallback or conditional inside validate_input() (or another helper shared by user/DHCP/reauth steps) while the test diff only touches the user or discovery flow.

candidates.rule: A coordinator that translates one client exception must translate all of the client errors its calls can raise, including aiohttp.ClientConnectionError.
candidates.trigger: _async_update_data adds an `except ClientResponseError` branch raising a translated UpdateFailed while other aiohttp errors reachable from the same call stay unhandled.

candidates.rule: Match todo items by casefolding both the requested value and the stored uid/summary rather than comparing against a tuple of raw values.
candidates.trigger: An intent or service handler comparing a user-supplied item against todo_item.uid / todo_item.summary with `in (...)`.

candidates.rule: Set _attr_unique_id once in __init__ from identifiers known at setup; never assign or recompute it inside update() or a coordinator callback.
candidates.trigger: An assignment to self._attr_unique_id (or self.entity_id-derived ids) inside update(), async_update(), or _handle_coordinator_update().

candidates.rule: Entity descriptions must be defined inside the integration; map external quirk/library keys onto Home Assistant owned EntityDescription objects instead of synthesizing descriptions from library data.
candidates.trigger: A helper that constructs an EntityDescription with key=<library quirk attribute> from an object supplied by the vendor library or quirks registry.

candidates.rule: When a Tuya device category is aliased to another category on one platform, add the same alias on every platform that already supports that category.
candidates.trigger: A new DeviceCategory entry added to a platform description map without the matching CATEGORY[DeviceCategory.X] = CATEGORY[DeviceCategory.Y] alias present in the sibling platforms.

candidates.rule: Factor repeated per-platform quirk registry lookup and entity construction into a shared helper module rather than copying the pattern into each platform.
candidates.trigger: A third or later platform file adding its own _get_quirk_entities() with the same TUYA_QUIRKS_REGISTRY.get_quirk_for_device + list comprehension shape.

candidates.rule: When one device yields several entities on the same platform, include a per-entity suffix in the unique_id so the entities cannot collide in the registry.
candidates.trigger: A list comprehension creating multiple entities of the same class from one device object where unique_id derives only from the device id.

candidates.rule: Unit conversion must run device-native to entity unit when reading a property and entity to device unit when writing, so set/read round-trips agree.
candidates.trigger: A TemperatureConverter.convert (or similar) call in a state property whose from/to arguments are the reverse of the matching call in async_set_*.

candidates.rule: Resolve an entity's native unit through the fixed precedence: no device_class first, then a device-reported unit, then NUMBER_DEVICE_CLASS_UNITS, then DEVICE_CLASS_UNITS, then the description default, and only finally drop the device_class.
candidates.trigger: A new branch inserted into _validate_device_class_unit or an equivalent unit-resolution routine ahead of the existing DEVICE_CLASS_UNITS checks.

candidates.rule: Energy sensor entity descriptions must set suggested_display_precision alongside native and suggested units so the registry options match the snapshots.
candidates.trigger: A SensorEntityDescription with device_class=SensorDeviceClass.ENERGY that sets native_unit_of_measurement but no suggested_display_precision.

candidates.rule: Annotate values that hold Home Assistant unit constants with their enum type (e.g. UnitOfTemperature) rather than str.
candidates.trigger: An attribute or return annotation typed str while the value comes from hass.config.units.temperature_unit or a UnitOfTemperature member.

candidates.rule: Name and translate a config switch after the setting it toggles, not after the action the underlying device performs.
candidates.trigger: A SwitchEntityDescription with entity_category=CONFIG whose translation_key reads as an imperative action (trigger_*, start_*) for a device capability that is merely enabled.

candidates.rule: Add tests that make the integration library raise during an entity action and assert the resulting HomeAssistantError carries the expected translation_domain and translation_key.
candidates.trigger: A platform gains a try/except around a library call that raises HomeAssistantError with translation_domain/translation_key, with no matching failure test.

candidates.rule: Keep a pull request's contents aligned with its title and description; a manifest requirement bump must not be shipped under a feature title, nor a feature under a bump title.
candidates.trigger: A PR whose only code change is a requirements version bump in manifest.json while the title/description promise a new entity or feature.

candidates.rule: Numeric state validation for template entities must keep booleans invalid; test with type(result) in (int, float) instead of isinstance.
candidates.trigger: A numeric-state check in a template platform written as isinstance(result, (int, float)).

candidates.rule: Template entity setup helpers must raise or log when their backing option is unset instead of silently doing nothing.
candidates.trigger: setup_state_template() or a sibling setup_* helper on TemplateEntity/TriggerEntity that returns early when the corresponding _*_option attribute is None.

candidates.rule: Do not raise repair issues off a template render that failed; only compare against a successfully rendered result.
candidates.trigger: A repair issue (async_create_issue / async_create_*_issue) created after assigning `result or []` from a template render that can yield None.

candidates.rule: In config flow tests take the flow id from the result returned by start_reauth_flow rather than re-fetching it via hass.config_entries.flow.async_progress().
candidates.trigger: A test calls entry.start_reauth_flow(hass) and then asserts on async_progress() to obtain flows[0]["flow_id"].

candidates.rule: Pass hass as the first argument to ConfigEntry.async_create_background_task, or use hass.async_create_background_task when entry lifecycle tying is not needed.
candidates.trigger: entry.async_create_background_task( called with only a coroutine and a name.

candidates.rule: Trigger entry reloads from coordinator/runtime callbacks with hass.config_entries.async_schedule_reload, and update the tracked baseline so the condition cannot re-fire.
candidates.trigger: A coordinator update handler that compares against cached known_* state and schedules hass.config_entries.async_reload on every difference.

candidates.rule: Only pass translation_placeholders that the referenced translation string actually consumes, and do not source them from library exception attributes that may not exist.
candidates.trigger: UpdateFailed/HomeAssistantError raised with translation_placeholders whose keys do not appear in the integration's strings.json entry, or built from e.message.

candidates.rule: Code reachable when the integration runs in public-API-only mode must not read the private bootstrap; resolve the needed identity at setup or omit the optional field.
candidates.trigger: An entity constructor or DeviceInfo build that dereferences api.bootstrap (e.g. via_device=(DOMAIN, self.data.api.bootstrap.nvr.mac)) on a path also used by API-key-only clients.

candidates.rule: Device-added dispatch must have a public-only equivalent when the integration supports API-key-only clients, covered by a test that starts with an empty bootstrap and then receives an add frame.
candidates.trigger: A websocket add/adopt handler that only dispatches objects tracked from the private bootstrap (e.g. _pending_camera_ids) while a public bootstrap can also produce add frames.

candidates.rule: Directional transitional states must map to distinct icons in icons.json, matching how cover distinguishes opening from closing.
candidates.trigger: An icons.json state block that adds both `opening` and `closing` (or equivalent paired transitional states) pointing at the same mdi icon.

candidates.rule: Do not feature-detect attributes on the integration's own pinned library with hasattr/getattr/callable; the manifest requirement pins the version, so call the API directly.
candidates.trigger: A setup or platform filter such as `if callable(getattr(node, "method", None))` applied to objects from the integration's requirement package.

candidates.rule: Diagnostics output should expose internal library and connection data that is not otherwise reachable, not a dump of device and entity registry information.
candidates.trigger: async_get_config_entry_diagnostics building lists of device names with their entities from the device/entity registry.

candidates.rule: Set only the _attr_* entity attributes; do not additionally assign the legacy private counterparts such as _name alongside _attr_name.
candidates.trigger: An entity __init__ assigning both self._attr_name and self._name (or another duplicated legacy attribute) to the same value.

candidates.rule: Every translation_key referenced by an entity must have a matching entity name entry in strings.json; do not remove a name while the key is still used.
candidates.trigger: A strings.json diff deleting the `name` under an entity translation key whose description still sets translation_key.

candidates.rule: When a tri-state device value (True/False/None) selects an entity's identity or translation key, handle None explicitly instead of letting it fall into the false branch.
candidates.trigger: A conditional expression choosing between two translation keys or entity variants from a helper that can return None, written as `"a" if flag else "b"`.

candidates.rule: Entities whose state is bool | None need tests that separate missing data (unknown) from an explicit zero/false reading.
candidates.trigger: A new is_on/native_value property returning None for absent data and a boolean otherwise, with fixtures covering only the populated case.

candidates.rule: Normalize loosely typed device API values explicitly: compare feature flags and on/off states against the full set of representations the API uses (True, 1, "1") instead of relying on truthiness or a partial literal set.
candidates.trigger: Entity gating written as `if not all(coordinator.get_value(path) ...)` or a state check written as `value in (True, "1")` against a JSON API that also returns ints and numeric strings.

candidates.rule: A select entity's current_option must always be one of its advertised options; fall back to a valid option and log when the device reports an unknown value.
candidates.trigger: self._attr_current_option assigned from a dict .get() lookup keyed on a device-supplied value, with no handling of the None result.

candidates.rule: Collections surfaced to the frontend (select options, websocket payloads) must be ordered deterministically, e.g. sorted, rather than inheriting dict or matcher load order.
candidates.trigger: _attr_options or a websocket command response built by iterating a library dict, registry, or matcher list without an explicit sort.

candidates.rule: Entity availability must follow both the coordinator's last_update_success and the continued presence of the backing object in the current bootstrap, not just incoming websocket messages.
candidates.trigger: An entity that subscribes to per-object websocket updates and sets _attr_available = data.last_update_success inside that callback, without a subscription to coordinator status or a presence check for the object.

candidates.rule: A translated UpdateFailed must use a translation key written for the update path and pass the underlying error text as the placeholder, never a hardcoded generic string.
candidates.trigger: _async_update_data raising UpdateFailed with a translation_key borrowed from a service/action error and translation_placeholders set to a literal message.

candidates.rule: entity_registry_enabled_default must be decided from the entity's identity, not from whether the device currently reports a value for it.
candidates.trigger: dataclasses.replace(description, entity_registry_enabled_default=...) combining a key check with description.value_fn(data) is not None.

candidates.rule: async_turn_on must never write a device value that switches the device off; clamp a brightness of 0 to the minimum non-zero value or reject it.
candidates.trigger: A light async_turn_on that converts ATTR_BRIGHTNESS with brightness_to_value and guards the minimum with a truthiness check such as `if brightness:`.

candidates.rule: Integration entity description subclasses must only add new fields; do not re-declare attributes the base EntityDescription already provides, such as SelectEntityDescription.options.
candidates.trigger: A frozen dataclass extending a platform EntityDescription that declares a field with the same name as one defined on the base class.

candidates.rule: Intent handlers must catch HomeAssistantError/ServiceValidationError specifically and re-raise IntentHandleError chained with `from err`, never a broad except with `from None`.
candidates.trigger: An intent handler wrapping a service call in `except Exception` and raising IntentHandleError with a formatted message and `from None`.

candidates.rule: Declare list-valued service schema fields with a real voluptuous list validator such as vol.All(cv.ensure_list, [str]), never with a bare Python type annotation like list[str].
candidates.trigger: A vol.Schema in an integration's services.py using a typing construct (list[str], dict[str, str]) as the validator for a Required/Optional key.

candidates.rule: Resolve a config entry from a service call with the core helper homeassistant.helpers.service.async_get_config_entry instead of hand-rolling entry-exists / correct-domain / loaded-state checks in the integration.
candidates.trigger: An integration service handler defining its own _async_get_config_entry-style function that looks up hass.config_entries by id and raises ServiceValidationError for missing/unloaded entries.

candidates.rule: Gate a report_usage deprecation warning on the deprecated condition actually being present, so callers that do not use the deprecated pattern never see it logged.
candidates.trigger: A report_usage call with breaks_in_ha_version placed on a common code path in core helpers without a check that the deprecated feature is in use.

candidates.rule: Keep a guard that prevents a registry's _async_load from running more than once.
candidates.trigger: Removal of the loaded-event assertions or any other once-only guard from a registry _async_load in homeassistant/helpers.

candidates.rule: Do not assume a sibling registry is set up when one registry helper calls another; guard dr.async_get / er.async_get so lookups still work with mocked or partially initialised registries.
candidates.trigger: A new dr.async_get(self._hass) or er.async_get(hass) call added inside an entity_registry or device_registry method that previously touched only its own data.

candidates.rule: Do not key a long-lived registry or cache by entity_id; entity_id changes at runtime on registry rename, so track the key used at insert time or keep it in sync on entity_id updates.
candidates.trigger: A module-level or hass-data dict indexed by entity.entity_id in async_added_to_hass and deleted by entity.entity_id in async_will_remove_from_hass.

candidates.rule: Match entity registry entries on domain and platform in addition to unique_id; unique_id alone is not unique across integrations.
candidates.trigger: An entity_registry_updated event handler or registry lookup whose condition tests only entry.unique_id against a set of known ids.

candidates.rule: Keep the dependency between core helper modules one-way: do not add a top-level import that closes a cycle between helpers modules; use a function-local import or move the logic into the module that already owns the dependency.
candidates.trigger: A new top-level `from .<helper> import ...` in homeassistant/helpers/ where the imported module already imports the importing one.

candidates.rule: Use plain string values, not enum members, in selector option and mode lists so voluptuous validation errors show the user-facing string rather than an enum repr.
candidates.trigger: A selector constant in homeassistant/helpers/selector.py listing StrEnum members that are later fed to vol.In or exposed in a selector config.

candidates.rule: When an entity platform method maps a Home Assistant enum value onto a vendor constant, validate membership before indexing and raise HomeAssistantError, so an unsupported mode never escapes as a raw KeyError.
candidates.trigger: An async_set_* entity method indexing a module-level HA-to-vendor mapping dict (e.g. HVAC_TO_WF_MODE[hvac_mode]) inside a try block that only catches library or ValueError exceptions.

candidates.rule: Do not add strings.json entries or icons for preset modes that already exist as core common presets; use the core PRESET_* constants in code and let the built-in translations and icons apply.
candidates.trigger: New state_attributes.preset_mode entries in an integration's strings.json or icons.json naming standard presets such as eco, comfort, away, boost.

candidates.rule: Do not create entities for static device metadata; firmware version, mDNS name and similar constants belong in the device registry entry, not in the state machine.
candidates.trigger: A new sensor entity description whose value is a device identity or configuration constant (firmware version, mdns name, serial, IP) rather than a changing measurement, even under EntityCategory.DIAGNOSTIC.

candidates.rule: Key an entity's icons.json entry by the exact translation_key set on its entity description, not by the sensor's internal key.
candidates.trigger: An added icons.json entity key under a platform that does not literally match the translation_key of the corresponding EntityDescription.

candidates.rule: Bound any integration-held cache keyed by a client- or peer-supplied identifier with a global cap or TTL, not just a per-key size limit.
candidates.trigger: A dict on an integration object indexed by an externally supplied id (session id, request id) that is written on inbound messages and only pruned per entry.

candidates.rule: Reuse the integration's existing const.py constant when another platform module already defines the same tuning value; do not repeat the literal in a second platform.
candidates.trigger: A numeric literal in an integration platform module (delay, timeout, threshold) duplicating a value already named in that integration's const.py or another platform file.

candidates.rule: Include the idle notification value 0 in not_states for Z-Wave notification binary sensors so the entity clears when the device reports idle.
candidates.trigger: A NotificationZWaveJSEntityDescription whose not_states set lists only the specific event enum members and omits 0.

candidates.rule: Adding a NewZWaveDiscoverySchema for a value that a legacy DISCOVERY_SCHEMAS entry already matches must preserve the existing entities: set allow_multi and adjust the legacy catch-all's not_states, or migrate the whole notification type and add it to MIGRATED_NOTIFICATION_TYPES.
candidates.trigger: A new NewZWaveDiscoverySchema entry in zwave_js covering a notification value or command class that legacy discovery schemas already produce entities for.

candidates.rule: When deprecating a Python dependency, update DEPRECATED_PACKAGES in homeassistant/requirements.py and the FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES entry in script/hassfest/requirements.py together, including the replacement package named in the reason text.
candidates.trigger: A change to the DEPRECATED_PACKAGES dict in homeassistant/requirements.py with no matching change to FORBIDDEN_PACKAGES in script/hassfest/requirements.py.

candidates.rule: Keep the pylint plugin README's description of a checker's accepted and rejected patterns exactly in step with the checker implementation and its test cases.
candidates.trigger: A change to pylint/plugins/README.md or a checker module docstring describing which code shapes the checker accepts, without a matching implementation or test in pylint/plugins/pylint_home_assistant/checkers/.

candidates.rule: Drive a test's expected end state with a realistic mock sequence (raise once, then return data) rather than an always-raising mock that reaches the expected state only through internal retry or swallowing.
candidates.trigger: A test parametrized over ConfigEntryState.LOADED whose client mock has an unconditional side_effect exception on the data-fetch method.

candidates.rule: Use the integration's DOMAIN constant wherever the domain appears, including as the key of the configuration dict passed to async_setup_component, rather than repeating the domain string.
candidates.trigger: A hardcoded domain string in a test or component module that already imports DOMAIN, e.g. async_setup_component(hass, DOMAIN, {"counter": {...}}).

candidates.rule: Do not stack repeated await hass.async_block_till_done() calls to make a fixture settle; use a single deterministic wait or document why more than one pass is required.
candidates.trigger: Two or more consecutive `await hass.async_block_till_done()` statements in a test or conftest fixture.

candidates.rule: Mock an integration's library with AsyncMock-based fixtures rather than hand-written fake client classes.
candidates.trigger: A new conftest.py defining a stub class that reimplements the vendor library's properties and setters instead of patching the client with AsyncMock.

candidates.rule: When core code branches on whether the caller is a built-in integration (module starting with homeassistant.components.), test both the warning branch and the suppression branch.
candidates.trigger: A new report/warning in homeassistant/ that is skipped for modules under homeassistant.components., with tests asserting only the warning case.

candidates.rule: Custom pylint checkers that recognise service registrations must handle the service_func= keyword form as well as the positional argument, for both async_register and async_register_admin_service.
candidates.trigger: A checker helper in pylint/plugins that extracts a handler from hass.services.async_register / async_register_admin_service using only call.args positional indexes.

candidates.rule: Narrow custom pylint checks so they fire only on the exact pattern they target; a check on exception construction must require a literal string or f-string message, not merely the presence of a positional argument.
candidates.trigger: A checker condition of the form `if node.args and not has_translation_key` (or similar) that inspects only argument count rather than the argument node type.

candidates.rule: Keep file-glob constants in script/ tooling identical to the paths: filter of the GitHub workflow that invokes them.
candidates.trigger: A TRACKED_PATTERNS-style glob tuple in script/ that is narrower than the paths: filter of the corresponding .github/workflows/*.yml.

candidates.rule: New hassfest validation must ship with hassfest tests exercising both the valid case and each distinct failure mode it can report.
candidates.trigger: A new validation branch in script/hassfest/*.py that adds an error message, with no corresponding case added under tests/hassfest/.

candidates.rule: When a config flow gains a fallback path, add a test for its success case end to end, not only for the error case that motivated it.
candidates.trigger: A new branch in an integration's config_flow.py that calls the client on a cache miss, with test_config_flow.py changes covering only the failure outcome.

candidates.rule: When a platform converts raw API values into device_class or state_class enums, add a test feeding a missing or invalid value and assert setup does not raise and the entity is still created with the attribute unset.
candidates.trigger: New SensorDeviceClass/SensorStateClass enum lookups on payload data in an integration's sensor.py, with tests covering only well-formed payloads.

candidates.rule: Do not assert exact library call counts during setup; assert the resulting device and entity registry state instead.
candidates.trigger: An assertion of the form `assert mock_client.<method>.call_count == N` in an integration test covering config entry setup.

candidates.rule: Test module and test function docstrings must name the platform and behaviour actually under test; update them when the parametrization or the file's subject changes.
candidates.trigger: A new or copied test file whose module docstring names a different platform than the file tests, or a parametrized test whose docstring describes only a subset of the cases in its params list.

candidates.rule: Match the mock type to the real callable: patch awaited functions with AsyncMock (or new_callable=AsyncMock) and synchronous ones with MagicMock, and never spec a whole library model object as AsyncMock when it exposes synchronous listener/registration methods.
candidates.trigger: A test adds `patch(...)` / `AsyncMock(spec=...)` / a fixture annotation whose sync-vs-async kind does not match the awaited-ness of the patched target in the integration code.

candidates.rule: Tests must reuse the integration's own constants and helper functions (homeassistant.const constants, config keys, identifier helpers) instead of repeating string literals or re-deriving the value in the test.
candidates.trigger: A test or conftest introduces a raw string literal such as "unavailable" or "device_id", or recomputes an identifier inline, where the integration code uses STATE_UNAVAILABLE, CONF_DEVICE_ID or a helper like get_camera_identifier.

candidates.rule: Stateless entity triggers must accept STATE_UNKNOWN as a valid from_state so the first real event after startup fires, matching button entity trigger semantics.
candidates.trigger: A trigger implementation or its parametrized tests treat an `unknown` -> first-matching-state transition as not triggering for a stateless domain (event, button).

candidates.rule: Service actions that resolve a device_id must have test coverage for the device being absent from the device registry, and should raise ServiceValidationError rather than failing silently.
candidates.trigger: A new service handler takes `device_id` and looks it up in the device registry, with tests only covering the happy path and backend errors.

candidates.rule: Assert that a specific mocked method was or was not awaited instead of inspecting `mock.mock_calls[-1]`.
candidates.trigger: A test indexes into `mock_calls` (e.g. `mock_calls[-1][0] != "send_start_impulse_async"`) to prove a call did not happen.

candidates.rule: Parametrized tests for capability/feature flag enums must cover the combined-flags and zero/empty value, not only the single-flag cases.
candidates.trigger: A platform change alters how bitwise capability flags are interpreted while the test parametrization lists only individual enum members.

candidates.rule: Do not hard-code generated entity_ids in tests; resolve the entity through the entity registry by unique_id or config entry and assert on the resolved id.
candidates.trigger: A test contains a literal entity_id string such as "sensor.fresh_r_inside_temperature" built from a device name slug.

candidates.rule: Assert that `hass.states.get(entity_id)` returned a state object before dereferencing `.state`.
candidates.trigger: A test chains `hass.states.get(...).state` in an assertion or comprehension without a preceding `is not None` check.

candidates.rule: Every parameter of a test function, including injected fixtures, must carry a type annotation.
candidates.trigger: A new `async def test_*` adds a fixture parameter (e.g. `mock_growatt_v1_api`) with no annotation while its siblings are annotated.

candidates.rule: When new entities are added, regenerate and commit the snapshot files, and keep any hard-coded expected entity list in the same order the entity descriptions are iterated during setup.
candidates.trigger: A PR adds entity descriptions to a platform's description tuple and adds matching entries to a test's expected-entity list or snapshot assertion.

candidates.rule: Fixture payloads and mocked client return values must mirror the real upstream API's shape and key casing, not the post-processed form the integration produces.
candidates.trigger: A JSON fixture uses already-normalised keys (snake_case where the API sends camelCase), or a mock client method coerces/drops payload shapes the real library returns.

candidates.rule: Do not land conftest fixtures or helpers that no test in the same PR uses; add them with the follow-up PR that needs them.
candidates.trigger: A conftest.py gains fixtures (coordinators, clients, init_*_integration helpers) that are not referenced by any test file in the diff.

candidates.rule: Shared mock/data construction repeated across tests belongs in a pytest fixture in conftest.py, not in module-level builder functions each test calls manually.
candidates.trigger: A test module defines a helper like `build_homeegrams()` or inline mock-client wiring and calls it in an identical setup block before `setup_integration` in several tests.

candidates.rule: Timestamps passed to `freezer.move_to()` must carry an explicit timezone offset when the assertions depend on local-time conversion.
candidates.trigger: A test calls `freezer.move_to("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS")` with no `Z`/`+00:00` suffix while the code under test branches on `dt_util.now().hour`.

candidates.rule: After firing a coordinator's update timer with `async_fire_time_changed`, await `hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)` before asserting on refreshed state.
candidates.trigger: A test ticks the freezer by the coordinator UPDATE_INTERVAL, calls `async_fire_time_changed`, then asserts entity state after a plain `await hass.async_block_till_done()`.

candidates.rule: Run the translation generation script for the integration and re-capture entity snapshots after adding translation keys, so snapshotted entities show their translated names and object-id-derived entity_ids.
candidates.trigger: A snapshot .ambr adds entities with a `translation_key` set but `original_name: None`, no `object_id_base`, and generic entity_ids like `sensor.device_1_2`.

candidates.rule: Deprecation repair issues must have test coverage for every branch that selects a different translation key, including the entity-used-in-automations/scripts variant and its placeholder substitution.
candidates.trigger: A repairs test only covers the plain deprecated-entity issue while the implementation also raises a `*_scripts`/`*_automations` variant with an `{items}` placeholder.

candidates.rule: When a change tightens validation, fix the existing tests it breaks instead of deleting them.
candidates.trigger: A diff that adds stricter validation also removes an existing test function.

candidates.rule: When a service response model gains fields, add a test case where those fields carry non-default values rather than only the default None case.
candidates.trigger: A test's expected service-response dict gains new keys whose asserted values are all `None`.

candidates.rule: A test parametrized over a fixture-overriding value must declare that fixture as a function parameter.
candidates.trigger: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("mqtt_config_entry_data", ...)` (or another fixture-override parametrization) sits above a test whose signature omits that name.

candidates.rule: Unique_id migration tests must round-trip every unique_id format the integration produces (device, multi-channel and group variants) and must not let one format's pattern match another's ids.
candidates.trigger: A migration test derives old-format unique_ids with string slicing/suffix matching and skips entries where the channel is None.

candidates.rule: Conditions and triggers that filter their targets by supported domain need a negative test proving the condition does not pass when only unsupported entities are targeted.
candidates.trigger: A new condition/trigger test file covers only supported entity domains, including a `behavior='all'` case.

candidates.rule: Matter node fixtures must list any cluster whose attributes they define in that endpoint's Descriptor ServerList.
candidates.trigger: A `tests/components/matter/fixtures/nodes/*.json` adds attributes for a cluster id that is absent from the endpoint's `65531` server list.

candidates.rule: Do not snapshot volatile numeric sensor readings; snapshot the stable entity metadata (entity id, device class, unit, availability) and relax the fluctuating `state` value.
candidates.trigger: A dependency bump changes numeric `state` values inside a snapshot .ambr file, forcing snapshot churn.

candidates.rule: Snapshot the device registry entry once per test module, not once per entity.
candidates.trigger: A per-platform test loops over entity registry entries and snapshots the resolved `device_entry` inside the loop.

candidates.rule: A regenerated snapshot must contain exactly one entity per unique_id for a config entry; prune stale blocks instead of committing duplicates.
candidates.trigger: A snapshot .ambr contains two entries sharing a unique_id under different entity_ids.

candidates.rule: A test must actually exercise the failure path named in its name and docstring; patch the dependency with a failing `side_effect` rather than a benign empty result that duplicates an existing test.
candidates.trigger: A config flow test named for a startup/discovery failure patches the discovery helper to return an empty result and asserts a generic abort reason.

candidates.rule: Tests that enable a disabled-by-default entity must advance time to run the coordinator refresh and assert the entity's resolved value, not merely that the entity exists.
candidates.trigger: A test enables an entity via the entity registry and reloads, then only asserts `state is not None`.

candidates.rule: Obtain registries through the provided pytest fixtures (`entity_registry: er.EntityRegistry`, `device_registry`, `issue_registry`) declared as test/fixture parameters, not by calling `er.async_get(hass)` inside the body.
candidates.trigger: A test or conftest fixture body calls `er.async_get(hass)` / `dr.async_get(hass)` instead of taking the registry fixture.

candidates.rule: Assert that entities were not created by querying the entity registry for the config entry (by unique_id or original_name) rather than by guessing generated entity_id slugs.
candidates.trigger: A test asserts `hass.states.get("<domain>.<guessed_slug>") is None`, especially for names containing characters that alter slugging (e.g. "2+", "2-way").

candidates.rule: Assert that a specific repair issue key is absent rather than that the whole issue registry is empty.
candidates.trigger: A test asserts `len(issue_registry.issues) == 0` or compares the full issue registry contents.

candidates.rule: Setup-failure tests must assert the exception whose retry semantics match the intent: ConfigEntryNotReady when setup should be retried, ConfigEntryError when the failure is fatal.
candidates.trigger: A test named or documented as "not ready" asserts ConfigEntryError (or vice versa) around async_setup_entry.

candidates.rule: Tests must reference the integration's own constants for config entry data and option keys instead of repeating raw string literals.
candidates.trigger: A test passes a bare string key into options={...} or data={...} of a config entry where the integration's const.py defines a constant for it.

candidates.rule: Every translation_key introduced by an entity must have a matching entry added to the integration's strings.json in the same PR.
candidates.trigger: A new entity description or renamed entity appears in code/snapshots without a corresponding key under entity in strings.json.

candidates.rule: Entity-platform tests must assert the exact expected entity count (or snapshot the entities), never a loose lower bound.
candidates.trigger: assert len(states) >= N in a platform test, especially where a nearby comment claims a precise entity count.

candidates.rule: Media source tests must construct MediaSourceItem with the integration's own DOMAIN and a bare item identifier, not another integration's domain or a full media-source:// URI.
candidates.trigger: MediaSourceItem(hass, "<other-domain>", f"{media_source.URI_SCHEME}{DOMAIN}", ...) in a media source test.

candidates.rule: Recorder platform unit-conversion maps must be string-to-string; do not use None keys or empty-string units in the mapping.
candidates.trigger: A recorder platform test or implementation supplies a unit map entry like {None: ""} where the annotation is dict[str, dict[str, str]].

candidates.rule: Syrupy snapshot names must be regenerated from the actual parametrization ids rather than hand-written, so they match the parameter values exactly.
candidates.trigger: A hand-edited .ambr entry whose bracketed id (e.g. [megane_e-tech]) differs from the parametrize source values (megane_e_tech).

candidates.rule: Tests must not mutate a shared module-level CONFIG dict; copy it and set options on the nested integration config the integration actually reads.
candidates.trigger: A test assigns into a module-level CONFIG constant (config[CONF_X] = ...) rather than building a local copy of the nested domain config.

candidates.rule: A test's name and docstring must describe exactly the behavior it asserts; when they disagree with the assertions or with the PR's stated behavior, one of them is wrong and must be corrected before merge.
candidates.trigger: A test docstring describes a different outcome, service, or exception than the assertions in its body (including copied docstrings from a neighboring test).

candidates.rule: Service-call tests must pass values that are valid under the service schema (the integration's direction/mode constants), not stand-in primitives.
candidates.trigger: A test invokes an integration service or helper with integers/placeholders where the service schema expects domain constants such as DIR_LEFT/DIR_UP.

candidates.rule: Bluetooth integration tests must drive the integration through the public injection helpers (e.g. inject_bluetooth_service_info) rather than calling a coordinator's private _async_handle_bluetooth_event.
candidates.trigger: A test calls coordinator._async_handle_bluetooth_event(...) or another underscore-prefixed coordinator callback to simulate an advertisement.

candidates.rule: Do not re-serialize existing JSON test fixtures; leave non-ASCII text as literal UTF-8 rather than \u escapes.
candidates.trigger: A diff in tests/components/*/fixtures/*.json rewrites accented characters as \uXXXX escapes or otherwise reformats untouched fixture lines.

candidates.rule: Tests must not assert known-incorrect integration behavior as the expected value; leave the assertion out or mark it xfail until the integration is fixed.
candidates.trigger: A parametrized test case is accompanied by a comment calling the expected value a known bug or a follow-up fix.

candidates.rule: Patch third-party helpers at the integration's import site (homeassistant.components.<domain>.<name>) rather than patching the library or stdlib module globally.
candidates.trigger: A test calls patch("shutil.which", ...) or patch("<library>.<func>", ...) for a symbol the integration imported into its own module namespace.

candidates.rule: Do not add test fixtures - JSON fixture files, conftest fixtures, or fixture parameters in a test signature - that no test actually consumes.
candidates.trigger: A PR adds a file under tests/components/*/fixtures/, a fixture in conftest.py, or a parameter such as snapshot to a test signature that is never referenced.

candidates.rule: Give each entity a translation_key so its name (and therefore its entity_id suffix) is distinct from the device name instead of the entity_id collapsing to button.<device>.
candidates.trigger: A new entity snapshot shows original_name/object_id_base as None and an entity_id equal to the bare device or container slug.

candidates.rule: Tests that expect a translated HomeAssistantError must assert translation_domain and translation_key on the raised exception, not merely that some HomeAssistantError was raised.
candidates.trigger: pytest.raises(HomeAssistantError) around a service call in a test that parametrizes a translation_key without asserting it.

candidates.rule: Import SnapshotAssertion from syrupy.assertion and snapshot_platform from tests.common; do not pull SnapshotAssertion out of tests.common.
candidates.trigger: A test file adds `from tests.common import SnapshotAssertion` (alone or alongside snapshot_platform).

candidates.rule: Keep a PR to its stated change; unrelated test improvements such as renaming fixtures or introducing parametrization belong in a separate PR.
candidates.trigger: A PR whose stated purpose is one small change also renames fixtures, restructures parametrization, or refactors unrelated tests in the same diff.

candidates.rule: Name a platform test after the Home Assistant service it calls rather than the underlying vendor concept.
candidates.trigger: A test that calls a service such as vacuum.clean_area is renamed to describe the implementation detail (test_clean_segments).

candidates.rule: Define a shared test constant once in a common test module; do not duplicate it across conftest.py and individual test files.
candidates.trigger: A constant such as TEST_TIMEZONE is added to conftest.py while an identical definition already exists in a test module of the same component.

candidates.rule: Advance coordinator intervals with freezer.tick(...) followed by async_fire_time_changed(hass); do not pass a separately computed dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta timestamp.
candidates.trigger: async_fire_time_changed(hass, dt_util.utcnow() + timedelta(...)) in a test that also uses the freezer fixture.

candidates.rule: Device fixtures must be exported from the actual target device so metadata (name, product_name, category) is consistent with the datapoints they declare.
candidates.trigger: A new tests/components/tuya/fixtures/*.json whose product name describes one device class while its DP set (e.g. weight, heart_rate) belongs to another.

candidates.rule: An empty-string unit from a device payload must be normalized to None (or mapped to a real unit) rather than surfacing as unit_of_measurement: ''.
candidates.trigger: A discovery path or fixture carries "unit": "" for a numeric datapoint and passes it through to the entity description.

candidates.rule: Tests that assert on debug log output must raise the level first with caplog.set_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="homeassistant.components.<domain>").
candidates.trigger: A test asserts a debug-level message appears in caplog.text without calling caplog.set_level for the integration's logger.

candidates.rule: Read entity metadata that is not exposed in the state through the entity registry, not by reaching into hass.data["entity_components"].
candidates.trigger: A test does hass.data["entity_components"]["<platform>"].get_entity(entity_id) to inspect an entity object.

candidates.rule: When an entity key change alters generated entity_ids, update every remaining reference to the old entity_id in the test module.
candidates.trigger: A parametrization renames sensor keys (device_cpu -> cpu) while other tests in the file still assert on the old entity_id string.

candidates.rule: A test parametrized over a payload fixture must request that fixture in its signature, otherwise drop the parametrization.
candidates.trigger: @pytest.mark.parametrize("clients_all_payload", [...]) on a test whose signature omits clients_all_payload.

candidates.rule: Never wait on wall-clock time with asyncio.sleep in tests; patch the delay or call_later so timers fire deterministically.
candidates.trigger: await asyncio.sleep(<n>) used to let a scheduled callback or timer fire in a test.

candidates.rule: Do not leave test fixtures or module-level test constants defined but never referenced; remove them or wire them into the tests that need them.
candidates.trigger: A conftest fixture or a TEST_* constant is added or left behind in a diff with no test referencing it.

candidates.rule: Assert against concrete expected values (such as the generated proxy URL prefix) rather than comparing two attributes of the object under test, which holds by construction.
candidates.trigger: assert obj.attr_a == obj.attr_b where both come from the same entity under test and the implementation makes them equal.

candidates.rule: Config entry migration tests must seed the entity registry with the entities a pre-migration install would already have, and assert they are re-associated with the new device or subentry.
candidates.trigger: A migration test asserts only that subentries/devices were created, without registering the old entities beforehand.

candidates.rule: Tests must not branch on entity_id with if/elif to pick expected values; parametrize the expected state alongside the entity or use the snapshot_platform helper.
candidates.trigger: An if/elif chain inside a test loop selecting which assertion to run per entity_id.

candidates.rule: Helpers that mutate a BluetoothServiceInfoBleak must copy the existing manufacturer_data mapping and update only the target manufacturer id, not replace the whole dict.
candidates.trigger: A bluetooth test helper builds `{<mfr_id>: bytes(...)}` and assigns it as the full manufacturer_data.

candidates.rule: Each device entry added to a shared API fixture must use a unique deviceId rather than reusing an existing device's identifier.
candidates.trigger: A new object appended to tests/components/*/fixtures/*.json repeats a deviceId already present in the file.

candidates.rule: Mock every API call the exercised code path makes, including calls whose exceptions the integration suppresses; follow the fixture combination already used in the integration's test_init.py.
candidates.trigger: A test adds one of a pair of related API fixtures (e.g. mock_setup_webhook) while leaving a sibling call (get_webhook_configuration) unmocked.

candidates.rule: Replacement functions substituted for a library API in tests must accept *args and **kwargs so they match the real call surface.
candidates.trigger: A test defines a zero-argument stub (e.g. an async generator) that replaces a library method the integration calls with arguments.

candidates.rule: Patch async library methods with new_callable=AsyncMock; a plain patch(..., return_value=...) yields a non-awaitable MagicMock.
candidates.trigger: patch("<library>.<Class>.<async_method>", return_value=...) without new_callable=AsyncMock in a conftest or test.

candidates.rule: A snapshot_platform test for a platform that contains entities with entity_registry_enabled_default=False must apply @pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default"), because snapshot_platform asserts disabled_by is None for every entity.
candidates.trigger: A new or edited test calls snapshot_platform(hass, entity_registry, snapshot, entry.entry_id) for a platform whose entity descriptions include entity_registry_enabled_default=False, without the entity_registry_enabled_by_default fixture.

candidates.rule: Syrupy .ambr snapshot files must be produced by running pytest --snapshot-update; never hand-edit them or hand-append snapshot blocks.
candidates.trigger: A diff adds or modifies lines inside a tests/components/*/snapshots/*.ambr file in a way that deviates from generator output, e.g. a duplicated '# ---' divider or a manually written EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot block.

candidates.rule: Test docstrings must state only the behavior under test; do not narrate device model history, the prior bug, or the PR description in them.
candidates.trigger: A new test's docstring spans multiple paragraphs describing a specific device firmware quirk, the exception it used to raise, or the regression history.

candidates.rule: Behavioral tests for a trigger must exercise every entity domain the trigger implementation accepts, not just one of them.
candidates.trigger: New tests for a zone/state/entity trigger parametrize over a single domain (e.g. "person") while the trigger's implementation also handles device_tracker or other domains.

candidates.rule: Changes to shared trigger/helper base classes must add coverage for subclasses that intentionally target STATE_UNKNOWN/STATE_UNAVAILABLE before excluding those states globally.
candidates.trigger: A diff makes an EntityTriggerBase-style helper skip unavailable/unknown states in match logic, and the accompanying tests only use an implementation whose is_valid_state() rejects those states.

candidates.rule: A fix for an async race must ship a regression test that actually drives both concurrent call paths; asserting a new private flag (e.g. script_obj._unloaded) does not substitute for reproducing the race.
candidates.trigger: A PR adds unload/teardown guard state to a helper and its test only asserts the private attribute instead of starting a run while the unload is in progress.

candidates.rule: Test cases added to the custom pylint quality-scale checkers must encode a rule the checker deliberately enforces; incidental matches produced by the implementation should be dropped or the implementation adjusted.
candidates.trigger: A new parametrized case in tests/pylint/quality_scale/ asserts a diagnostic on code whose flagged condition cannot occur in practice (e.g. _attr_unique_id assignment after a raise in __init__).

candidates.rule: Changes to the split_tests fixture-hashing logic must add coverage proving the hash changes when a shared helper module above or beside the chosen root is edited, not only for conftest.py files.
candidates.trigger: A diff modifies fixture-hash computation in script/split_tests and its tests only cover conftest.py edits and same-directory scope.

candidates.rule: End-to-end frontend tests must assert on the element of the specific step under test, not on the outer shell component that renders before its API call resolves.
candidates.trigger: A Playwright spec asserts only expect(page.locator("ha-onboarding")).toBeVisible() (or another shell element) after navigating, without waiting for the concrete step element.

candidates.rule: An entity registry snapshot whose 'aliases' field renders as list([None]) must be investigated as an entity-registration bug; aliases must be an empty set or a set of non-null strings.
candidates.trigger: A new .ambr snapshot contains "'aliases': list([\n None,\n ])" inside an EntityRegistryEntrySnapshot.

candidates.rule: A test that patches an API call to raise an authentication exception must assert that the reauth flow actually started (e.g. config_entry_reauth.assert_called_once()), not merely reference the mock.
candidates.trigger: A test injects an authentication exception via side_effect and references a reauth mock without calling an assertion method on it.

candidates.rule: Reconfigure-flow tests that submit only a subset of the config entry fields must assert that the omitted optional fields (credentials, tokens) are preserved on the entry.
candidates.trigger: A test_config_flow.py reconfigure test calls async_configure with a dict omitting CONF_USERNAME/CONF_PASSWORD or other optional entry keys and only asserts the flow result type.

candidates.rule: When firing async_fire_time_changed to trigger a coordinator refresh, capture the base time after the config entries are set up (or add a margin / use fire_all=True); a time captured before setup can land before the timer the entity scheduled.
candidates.trigger: A test assigns now = dt_util.now()/utcnow() before async_setup_component or hass.config_entries.async_setup, then calls async_fire_time_changed(hass, now + <scan interval>) and asserts on refresh call counts.

candidates.rule: A new mocked device/appliance fixture must configure every library accessor the integration's base entity reads, including the availability accessor, matching the sibling fixtures in the same conftest.
candidates.trigger: A conftest.py adds a Mock(spec=<device class>) fixture that sets some *.return_value attributes but omits one that existing fixtures for the same integration set (e.g. get_online.return_value = True).

candidates.rule: Config entry migration tests must be named (and their docstring worded) for the exact version transition exercised, e.g. test_migrate_minor_version_1_to_2 rather than test_migrate_to_1_1.
candidates.trigger: A test in tests/components/*/test_init.py exercises async_migrate_entry / minor_version or version bumps but its name does not state the source and target version.

candidates.rule: Fixtures that build a MockConfigEntry must derive its title, data and options from the parametrizable config fixture rather than hard-coding literals.
candidates.trigger: A conftest.py fixture constructs MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, title="<literal>", ...) while a sibling get_config/mock_config fixture supplies the same value and can be overridden by tests.

candidates.rule: Tests must address entities by their hard-coded entity ID (as captured in the snapshot) instead of looking the ID up dynamically from the entity registry.
candidates.trigger: A test calls er.async_entries_for_config_entry(...) and filters by domain/platform just to recover a single entity_id for a service call or state assertion.
